topics.topic: Whether a FlowConstant satisfies guard input availability or vacuous edge-only logic skips the node
questions: Does this test apply only to an input port that is supplied through one or more edges, or does a port supplied by a FlowConstant also satisfy “every incoming edge” when it has no incoming edges?
When an input port has no delivering edge but does have a FlowConstant, does that constant satisfy the port, or does the edge-only test still make the node `skipped_by_guard`?

How does this rule apply to an input port supplied by a FlowConstant, which has no incoming FlowEdge: does the constant count as an available delivery, or does the empty set of incoming edges make the port satisfy “every incoming edge” and skip the node?

quotes:
At start, each flow input's value is delivered along every edge from that
   input, and each constant to its port (constants were validated when the
   version was composed and proven, A05); an edge from a flow input straight to a flow output produces that
   output at once.

The next node is the ready node with the smallest node_id; a node is ready when every input port holds its value: flow inputs delivered along every edge from them — a flow input or flow output endpoint is the node whose node_id is the empty string (A05 rule 2), never the flow_id —, constants to their port — a FlowConstant's value is the value_id of the StoredValue composition wrote, delivered as a StoredValuesRef naming it, published again by nothing —, and outputs of a concluded succeeded node along every edge whose guard is absent or whose guard port value equals the guard value as canonical JSON text.
judgement.why: State 2 explicitly delivers each constant to its port and treats that delivery as satisfying readiness, so the empty-edge skip test does not vacuously skip a constant-supplied node.

topics.topic: Whether the empty string is reserved exclusively for flow-boundary endpoint identity
questions: Is the empty string reserved for flow-boundary endpoints and therefore forbidden as a FlowNode `node_id`, or may a node also have that identity?
May a FlowNode have the empty string as its `node_id`, which would make its edge endpoints indistinguishable from flow-level endpoints, or is the empty string reserved exclusively for flow endpoints?
Is the empty string forbidden as a FlowNode `node_id`, so it identifies only a flow-boundary endpoint?

judgement.divergence: One implementer refuses a FlowNode whose `node_id` is the empty string, reserving that identity for flow-boundary endpoints; another accepts it, making edges naming that node indistinguishable from boundary edges. The composing agent notices acceptance versus refusal, and run or proof callers notice different endpoint routing.
judgement.why: The text assigns the empty string to boundary endpoints but constrains node identifiers only to be unique, without saying whether that sentinel is forbidden for nodes.

topics.topic: Which unavailable-source conditions produce skipped_by_guard versus upstream_failed status
questions: Does “skipped node” mean only a source execution whose status is `skipped_by_guard`, or every source that was not executed, including one recorded `upstream_failed`?
What status is recorded when one required input port satisfies the new `skipped_by_guard` condition while another required input is unavailable because an upstream node failed?

Which upstream NodeExecution statuses make a source a “skipped node”: only `skipped_by_guard`, or also `upstream_failed`; and consequently should a downstream node whose input comes from an `upstream_failed` node be recorded `skipped_by_guard` or `upstream_failed`?

quotes:
A node an
   input of which comes from a failed node, or from a node itself
   `upstream_failed`, concludes `upstream_failed` without executing; when both
   rule 4 and this rule apply, this rule wins.

A node with one input from a failed node and another whose only edge is
   disabled by its guard concludes `upstream_failed`, not `skipped_by_guard`.
judgement.why: State 2 says an `upstream_failed` source propagates `upstream_failed`, and that failure propagation wins when the guard-skip condition also applies.

topics.topic: Whether composition supplies literal value data or an existing StoredValue value_id, and how identity and class are reconciled
questions: Does the compose request provide literal content, schema and class for the kernel to create or reuse a StoredValue and derive its `value_id`, or does it provide an existing `value_id`; and if an existing id is allowed, how is the separately declared class reconciled with the class already encoded in that id?

Does the compose action receive literal content, schema and class and have the kernel mint or reuse its StoredValue and `value_id`, or does it receive an already-existing `value_id`; if the latter, what does “written when the version is composed” mean?

quotes:
A flow constant is a typed literal
   (M16): the composing agent declares its `value_schema` with its class, and its
   StoredValue takes both. Composition refuses a constant whose value does not
   fit its declared schema (A05 rule 7); phase 2 of the proof checks that the
   declared schema is the target port's stored schema (M21), so the value then
   fits the port (A05 rule 1); the constant's identity does not depend on
   resolving another record.

compose_flow_version: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] Each constant becomes a StoredValue of value carriage with the declared value_schema and disclosure class, value_digest the content_identity of a BytesContent holding its bytes — the ConstantInput's canonical_json, already canonical bytes, used as they are — and value_id the content_identity of its StoredValueContent, its bytes stored with put_value_bytes, and a FlowConstant naming that value_id.

handle_compose_flow_version: [FIELD_PROJECTION] MUST turn each RequestConstant into a ConstantInput with the same to_node, to_port, canonical value_schema text and disclosure_class and with canonical_json set to the canonical bytes of its json_text.
judgement.why: State 6 specifies that composition receives literal JSON, schema and class, creates or reuses the content-addressed StoredValue, and stores its derived `value_id` in the FlowConstant.
